reference: GNU coreutils realpath is the independent parity oracle. Fixture scripts use only relative paths and create small files and symlinks under the runner's private /work tree. For the Bash-only -c option, the reference branch uses GNU realpath -e on an existing fixture path, which gives the comparable all-components-exist behavior. Bash-only array, verbose, and builtin help metadata are checked against the documented contract in stock-loadables/realpath.c.
coverage: Canonical output for relative paths containing dot and dot-dot components, including a path with a space in its name.
Resolution of a relative directory symlink and a symlink chain.
Lexical canonicalization with -s while a symlink component is present.
Existence checking through the loadable's -c option.
GNU's default handling of a missing final component and multiple operands with a missing parent.
No-operand usage behavior compared with GNU coreutils.
Bash builtin type/help metadata and the loadable-only -a, -q, and -v contracts.
exclusions: GNU-only realpath options such as -m, --relative-to, and -z are outside the Bash loadable's documented interface.
The loadable's -a array assignment and -v formatting have no GNU CLI equivalent, so they are contract cases rather than claimed GNU parity.
No privileged, hardware, network, or host-system path behavior is included; all operations use ordinary fixture paths.

cases.purpose: Canonicalizes existing relative paths with redundant dot and dot-dot components and preserves a filename containing spaces.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; os.makedirs("d/sub", exist_ok=True); open("d/file with space", "wb").close(); open("d/sub/item", "wb").close()'
cd d/sub
realpath '.././file with space' './item' '../../d/../d/sub/item'

cases.purpose: Follows a relative directory symlink and a second symlink whose target traverses the first link.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; os.makedirs("target/nested", exist_ok=True); open("target/nested/file", "wb").close(); os.symlink("target", "dirlink"); os.symlink("dirlink/nested/file", "chain")'
realpath dirlink/nested/file chain

cases.purpose: Checks -s lexical dot-dot removal without following a symlink component; the nested target makes following the link produce a different path.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; os.makedirs("real/deep", exist_ok=True); open("rootfile", "wb").close(); os.symlink("real/deep", "shortcut")'
realpath -s shortcut/../rootfile

cases.purpose: Exercises the loadable's -c existence check on an existing path and compares it with GNU realpath -e, the corresponding all-components-exist mode.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'open("present", "wb").close()'
kind=$(type -t realpath)
if [[ $kind == builtin ]]; then
  realpath -c present
elif [[ $kind == file ]]; then
  realpath -e present
else
  exit 99
fi

cases.purpose: Checks GNU coreutils' default handling of a missing final component. GNU canonicalizes this path successfully; the candidate's differing status and output are retained as a parity failure.
With multiple operands, emits canonical paths for successful operands before and after a path with a missing parent, then reports overall failure.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'open("first", "wb").close(); open("last", "wb").close()'
rc=0
realpath first missing-parent/absent last || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 ]] || exit 99
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Checks the no-operand error status and diagnostic presence against GNU coreutils; a status difference is retained as a compatibility failure.
Confirms realpath is registered as a Bash builtin and that help exposes the documented description and synopsis.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t realpath) == builtin ]] || exit 10
help realpath > help.txt
have_description=0
have_array_doc=0
have_strip_doc=0
while IFS= read -r line; do
  case $line in
    *'Display pathname in canonical form.'*) have_description=1 ;;
    *'The -a option stores each canonicalized PATHNAME argument'*) have_array_doc=1 ;;
    *'canonicalize . and .. pathname components'*) have_strip_doc=1 ;;
  esac
done < help.txt
[[ $have_description == 1 && $have_array_doc == 1 && $have_strip_doc == 1 ]] || exit 11
type -t realpath
printf 'help-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Checks documented -a indexed-array assignment, input order, symlink canonicalization, and that -q suppresses command output without suppressing assignment.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; os.makedirs("dir", exist_ok=True); open("dir/file", "wb").close(); os.symlink("dir/file", "alias")'
realpath -q -a resolved dir/file alias
[[ ${#resolved[@]} == 2 ]] || exit 10
[[ ${resolved[0]} == "$PWD/dir/file" ]] || exit 11
[[ ${resolved[1]} == "$PWD/dir/file" ]] || exit 12
printf 'count=%s\n%s\n%s\n' "${#resolved[@]}" "${resolved[0]#"$PWD"/}" "${resolved[1]#"$PWD"/}"

cases.purpose: Checks the documented -v prefix and canonical destination for one relative pathname.
Compare missing final components, trailing slashes, dangling links and non-directory prefixes.
cases.script:
mkdir real; printf x > regular; ln -s absent dangling; ln -s real/leaf nested
for p in absent absent/ missing/leaf dangling nested regular/child absent/..; do
 if value=$(realpath "$p"); then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
 printf '%s=%s:%s\n' "$p" "$rc" "$value"
done

cases.purpose: Compare lexical paths with missing, symlink and regular-file components.
cases.script:
printf x > regular; ln -s absent dangling; ln -s regular filelink
for p in absent missing/leaf dangling regular/child missing/../leaf regular/../leaf dangling/child filelink/child; do
 if value=$(realpath -s "$p"); then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
 printf '%s=%s:%s\n' "$p" "$rc" "$value"
done
